answer: Correlation pooling pays a farm of fake keys as one agent. Every epoch, each key's answers to 20 shared tasks are embedded, and any keys whose replies echo each other above 0.9 cosine similarity are merged into one cluster that splits a single reward. Payouts sit in a vault for 3 epochs, so a comet key that appears, earns, and vanishes is still clustered before its funds unlock. Because only divergent reasoning escapes the merge, 100 fakes must run 100 independent models, so the farm loses the shared-compute savings that made faking cheap.
